```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Use `oauth_db_libsql_api()` to run SQLite SQL against a remote libSQL or
compatible Turso endpoint. shinyOAuth manages the visitor's sign-in and
token renewal; the database endpoint checks their token and permissions.
This helper uses the Hrana HTTP API, without an additional R database driver.

A local SQLite file has no OAuth login. The endpoint must be a server
configured to accept the access tokens issued to your app.

## Choose a compatible token issuer

### Self-hosted libSQL

The tested open-source libSQL server, version 0.24.33, verifies Ed25519
signatures using `SQLD_AUTH_JWT_KEY_FILE` or `SQLD_AUTH_JWT_KEY`. Configure
the public verification key using the server's
[Docker authentication instructions](https://github.com/tursodatabase/libsql/blob/main/docs/DOCKER.md#authentication).
The app must obtain compatible database access tokens from its issuer.

Issue an explicit database namespace in `id`, permissions in `a` (`"ro"`
for read-only or `"rw"` for read/write), and an `exp` expiry. Do not rely
on omitted claims: the tested server defaults missing permissions to write
access and permits tokens without an expiry. Its newer `p` permission
format is another option; see the
[server token implementation](https://github.com/tursodatabase/libsql/blob/main/libsql-server/src/auth/user_auth_strategies/jwt.rs).

This configuration is not a general OIDC resource server. It has no
issuer/audience discovery settings or JWKS URL configuration like the
DuckDB quack_oauth server. The tested version rejects tokens with an `aud`
claim because no accepted audience is configured. Use a dedicated signing
key and restrict token issuance to this database and the intended users.
The issuer must support Ed25519 signing and the required database claims.
Existing Entra, Google or default Auth0 tokens cannot simply be reused.

If your identity provider cannot issue compatible database access tokens,
you need a separate authorization gateway or token-exchange service.
This helper does not mint database tokens or implement token exchange.

Put the server behind HTTPS. Pass `ca_bundle` for a private CA. On Windows,
the Docker acceptance test uses curl's OpenSSL backend for its temporary
CA bundle. If your curl/Schannel build rejects a supplied private CA, set
`CURL_SSL_BACKEND=openssl` before loading curl or shinyOAuthDB and restart R.
Keep certificate and hostname verification enabled.

### Turso Cloud external providers

Turso Cloud has a separate
[external authentication setup](https://docs.turso.tech/sdk/authorization/jwks).
Its current documentation lists Clerk and Auth0 as supported providers.
Register the provider's JWKS endpoint and use the Turso CLI to generate a
database-specific JWT claims template, then configure the provider to issue
those claims. Restrict the template to the required database and operations.

The resulting provider-issued access token goes directly to the database
endpoint. A Turso platform-management API token, a shared database token,
or an OIDC ID token does not represent the visitor's database authorization.
Confirm the selected provider flow supplies the compatible database access
token through shinyOAuth's `auth$connection`.

## Configure the app

Register an OAuth client with redirect URI `http://localhost:8100`. Request
the database's configured permissions and any provider-specific audience
parameter. `sqlite.read` below is an example OAuth scope that your issuer
must define; libSQL's `a` or `p` claims enforce database permissions.
Remove or replace that scope if your registration uses another scheme.

Save the following values in `.Renviron` and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
OAUTHDB_LIBSQL_ISSUER=https://your-provider.example.org/
OAUTHDB_LIBSQL_URL=libsql://your-database-your-org.turso.io
OAUTHDB_LIBSQL_AUDIENCE=your-provider-api-audience
```

The audience setting is for provider configurations such as Auth0 with
Turso Cloud. Leave it empty for a self-hosted issuer configured to issue
database tokens without an audience claim.

## A complete app

Replace the table name and scopes for your database. The provider's token
configuration must satisfy the requirements above before running the app.

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

audience <- Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_LIBSQL_AUDIENCE")
provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_LIBSQL_ISSUER"),
  extra_auth_params = if (nzchar(audience)) list(audience = audience) else list()
)
client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "sqlite.read")
)

ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
  actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
  tableOutput("rows")
), id = "auth", client = client)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  libsql <- oauth_db_libsql_api(
    auth$connection, url = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_LIBSQL_URL"),
    required_scopes = "sqlite.read"
  )
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    libsql$query("SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE country = :country LIMIT 20",
      parameters = list(country = "NL"))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port = 8100), uiPattern = ".*")
```

Run `shiny::runApp(port = 8100)`. The app waits for sign-in before sending
SQL and clears the output on sign-out. Request `offline_access` too if
your provider requires it to renew tokens.

## Parameters and result types

Use an unnamed list for positional `?` parameters, or a fully named list
for named parameters. Values travel separately from SQL; no interpolation
is needed.

```{r parameters}
libsql$query("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE country = ?", list("NL"))
libsql$execute("INSERT INTO events(value) VALUES (:value)", list(value = "signed in"))
libsql$query("SELECT ? AS exact_integer", list(I("9223372036854775807")))
libsql$query("SELECT ? AS bytes, ? AS missing", list(as.raw(c(0, 255)), NULL))
```

Ordinary character values bind as text. Logical values bind as integers
`1` or `0`, and `NULL` or scalar `NA` bind as SQL NULL. Numeric values must
be finite. Format dates and timestamps as strings in your database's format.

SQLite integers return as strings so all 64 bits survive. Floating-point
values remain numeric. Blobs are raw vectors in list columns. A column
containing different non-null SQLite types remains a list, including nulls.
All-null and empty columns use logical missing values and retain their names.

`query(..., raw = TRUE)` returns the validated Hrana statement result,
including column declarations, affected-row count and last inserted row ID.
`execute()` returns this metadata invisibly, without collecting result rows.

## Request lifetime

Each operation obtains a current token, opens a new stream, executes one
statement and closes the stream in the same HTTPS request. Calls do not
share transactions, temporary tables, pragmas or other connection state.
`BEGIN` and `COMMIT` across separate calls cannot form a transaction.
This helper does not expose a DBI connection, batch transactions, cursors
or embedded replicas.

Results arriving after an account change, lost required permissions,
sign-out or session end are discarded. SQL requests are never replayed,
including HTTP 401, timeouts and lost write responses. After an ambiguous
write failure, check the database before deciding whether to submit again.
A submitted statement may finish even if the Shiny session has ended.

The source checkout includes a
[libSQL Docker fixture](https://github.com/lukakoning/shinyOAuthDB/tree/main/integration/libsql-oauth).
Run `Rscript --vanilla tools/check-libsql-oauth.R` from the repository root
with Docker running and the test dependencies installed to check signed
tokens, permissions, TLS, bound values and lost write responses locally.
The fixture uses synthetic Shiny authorizations and does not test browser
sign-in or Turso Cloud.
